question: Can independent subcolony count error alone generate the observed within-island beta variability and the within-island > among-island hierarchy?
motivation: Independent census error among subcolonies can create apparent asynchrony that averages out when counts are summed. This diagnostic therefore tests whether the hierarchical variability result exceeds that mechanical expectation.

eligible_units.reason: Exactly the same stable-roster subset used by the frozen primary hierarchical decomposition.

latent_complete_synchrony_null.island_total_trajectory: Use each island's observed annual breeding-pair total as the frozen latent island trajectory.
latent_complete_synchrony_null.fixed_subcolony_share: For each island, estimate one time-invariant subcolony share q_j from that subcolony's pooled 1991-2017 breeding-pair count divided by the island pooled total.
latent_complete_synchrony_null.interpretation: Before observation error, every subcolony within an island is exactly proportional to the same island trajectory and therefore perfectly synchronous.

error_models.inheritance: Reuse without alteration the error family already frozen for the N_eff mechanical-coupling diagnostic.
error_models.independence: Observation draws are independent among subcolony-year cells conditional on the latent means.
error_models.positive_state_condition: For an island-year whose frozen observed island total is positive, redraw the complete subcolony count vector only if every simulated subcolony count is zero, matching the known-positive-state conditioning used in the existing N_eff count-error diagnostic.
error_models.zero_state_condition: Frozen zero island totals remain all-zero.
error_models.simulated_island_total: Sum the simulated subcolony counts; use these same simulated totals in the among-island beta calculation.

frozen_statistics.primary_raw_beta_within: Wang-Loreau beta transition from all 25 stable subcolonies to the three island totals.
frozen_statistics.secondary_detrended_median_ratio: Median across COR/HUM/LIT of within-island covariance beta divided by among-island covariance beta after linear detrending of log1p abundance.
frozen_statistics.secondary_growth_median_ratio: Median across COR/HUM/LIT of within-island covariance beta divided by among-island covariance beta for annual log1p growth.
frozen_statistics.descriptive_all_three_ordering: Fraction of simulations in which every eligible island has within-island beta greater than among-island beta.

decision_rule.raw_hierarchy_robust_to_fixed_error_fami: true only if both primary raw statistics have one-sided p <= 0.05 under all three inherited error models.

interpretation_boundary: The Gamma-Poisson CV10% and CV20% models are uncalibrated sensitivity models, not estimates of Palmer observer error.
Failure under CV20% does not show that the hierarchy is an artifact; it shows that the current data cannot exclude that level of independent multiplicative count error.
Passing Poisson or CV10% does not prove biological buffering.
Annual-growth and detrended analyses are non-additive sensitivities and do not restore the exact Wang-Loreau alpha/beta/gamma identity.
No causal spatial-insurance, dispersal, forecasting, or early-warning claim is licensed by this diagnostic.
